research_rationale: EO 13709 (Obama, signed 2015-10-02, 80 FR 60793, published 2015-10-07) amends Executive Order 10431 of January 19, 1953 (National Security Medal): section 1(a) restates section 2 of EO 10431 to say who may be awarded the medal, section 1(b) adds paragraphs 7 and 8 on recommendations and processing, section 2 supersedes the regulations governing the award issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 1953, and section 3 states general provisions (no impairment of agency authority or OMB functions, implementation consistent with law and appropriations, no private right). The dossier inventory held only the first sentence of section 1 (characters 859-1011), so the inventory is corrected with overrides to seven scopes covering the whole text from the policy sentence through section 3(c). The text sets no term or condition. The held U.S. Code prints EO 10431 as amended by section 1 of EO 13709, which shows the amendments are part of the current text, and prints a note on section 2; neither the Code, the eCFR search nor the Federal Register disposition notes show any later amendment or revocation. The order cites no statute as authority (President and Commander in Chief), so no authority statute needs checking. Section 2 is a one-time supersession that took effect on signing, since the order states no other effective date, and is recorded as exhausted by performance; its surviving consequence (the 1953 regulations remain superseded) is separate.
savings_reason: The amendments to EO 10431 stand as part of that order's current text and no later instrument ends them; the superseded 1953 regulations stay superseded. Nothing else remains to save.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end: sections 1 and 3 state no term or condition, and no held later order revokes or amends EO 13709 or restates EO 10431 again. Section 2 is ended only in the sense that its one-time supersession was performed on signing, 2015-10-02.
scope_check: Seven scopes: the policy sentence introducing the amendments, section 1(a) (restated section 2 of EO 10431), section 1(b) (new paragraphs 7 and 8), section 2 (supersession of the 1953 regulations), and section 3(a), 3(b) and 3(c) (general provisions). Under the owner strike-and-insert ruling the amendments continue as part of the amended order.
independent_command_check: The amendments in section 1 and the supersession in section 2 are independent: the amendments continue in the text of EO 10431 while the supersession was a one-time act. The general provisions are rules of construction that continue.
savings_check: The only savings question is the status of the superseded 1953 regulations, which the Code note records as superseded; no residual command exists.

research_rationale: EO 12549 (Reagan, signed 1986-02-18, 51 FR 6370, published 1986-02-21) establishes a government-wide system of debarment and suspension for nonprocurement programs: executive departments and agencies shall participate in the system and a debarment or suspension by one agency has government-wide effect (section 1(a)), the activities covered (section 1(b)) and the programs not covered, including procurement (section 1(c)); agencies shall follow government-wide criteria and minimum due process procedures (section 2(a)), report debarred and suspended participants (section 2(b)) and not allow a party excluded by any agency to participate except by written exception (section 2(c)); agencies shall issue implementing regulations consistent with OMB guidelines, with deadlines of four and twelve months from the guidelines (section 3); the Interagency Committee on Debarment and Suspension is constituted (section 4); OMB designates an agency to keep the exclusion list and chair the committee, with a first report due within two years (section 5); OMB may issue guidelines (section 6); and OMB reports to the President within three years (section 7). The dossier inventory numbered the clauses incorrectly (the section 2(c) text was labelled section 5, and section 3 and parts of sections 5 to 7 were mislabelled or merged), so the inventory is corrected with overrides to twelve scopes, one per paragraph or section, covering every operative part of the held text after the preamble. The held current sources show the order in effect: a note in the U.S. Code under 31 U.S.C. 6101 prints it and a statute enacted in 2008 and amended in 2011 and 2013 identifies the committee by reference to sections 4 and 5 of the order, and 2 CFR 180.110 in the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 still refers to exclusions under the order. EO 12689 (1989), which the Federal Register note lists as a cross-reference, extends government-wide effect of debarment to procurement and expressly refers to nonprocurement activities covered by EO 12549; it recites EO 12549 and does not amend or revoke it. EO 13904 (2020) also only recites EO 12549 as policy. The order cites no statute as authority (the Constitution and laws of the United States), so no authority statute needs checking. The deadlines in sections 3, 5 and 7 are deadlines, not ends; no held source dates performance of those one-time steps, so no end is recorded for them.
savings_reason: The order has no end, and the held sources show its system still in use; no revocation or amendment was found, so no residual exists beyond the operative clauses. Exclusions already imposed by agencies stand under the regulations that implement the order.

research_rationale: EO 12568 (Reagan, signed 1986-10-02, 51 FR 35497, published 1986-10-06) empowers the Secretary of Defense and, as designated by him, the Secretaries, Under Secretaries and Assistant Secretaries of the Military Departments to exercise the discretionary authority granted to the President by subsection 806(a)(2) of the Department of Defense Authorization Act of 1986 (Public Law 99-145) to give hiring preference in nonappropriated fund activities to qualified spouses of members of the Armed Forces stationed in the same area, for positions in wage grade UA-8 and below, equivalent positions and positions paid at hourly rates. The authority statute was replaced rather than repealed: section 568(d) of Pub. L. 104-106 (February 10, 1996), printed in the held U.S. Code notes to 10 U.S.C. 1784, provides that the order applies as if its reference to section 806(a)(2) referred to section 1784 of title 10, and the held current text of 10 U.S.C. 1784(a)(2) carries the same preference authority. The order also cites 3 U.S.C. 301, which is held and in force. The Code prints the order as a note with no ending statement; the Federal Register disposition notes list no amendment or revocation.
savings_reason: The order is a continuing delegation with no end; Congress in 1996 directed that it apply as if it referred to 10 U.S.C. 1784, and no later instrument ending it was found, so no residual exists beyond the operative clause.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end: the text sets no term or condition, and the repeal-and-replacement of the statutory reference was handled by Pub. L. 104-106 section 568(d), which keeps the order in effect rather than ending it.
scope_check: Single operative scope: the whole sole paragraph delegating the discretionary preference authority for nonappropriated fund positions to the Secretary of Defense and his designees.
independent_command_check: The empowerment of the Secretary of Defense and of the designated military department officials is one command; the preference authority itself is conferred by statute and is not a separate command of the order.
savings_check: No ending event, so no savings question arises.

research_rationale: EO 10834 (Eisenhower, signed 1959-08-21, 24 FR 6865, published 1959-08-25) was issued on the admission of Hawaii and prescribes the design of the flag with fifty stars (Part I: sections 1 to 3, with the position of stars and the proportions set out in an attachment made part of the order), the sizes of flags authorized for executive agencies and rules for their procurement (Part II: sections 21 to 25) and general provisions (Part III: section 31 making the flag of EO 10798 official until July 4, 1960 and the Part I flag official on that date, section 32 defining executive agencies, and section 33 revoking EO 10798). The dossier inventory omitted section 1, ran section 3 across about 7,900 characters of Federal Register front matter, split the section 21 size table into row fragments and omitted sections 22 to 24 and 31 to 32 as separate scopes, so the inventory is corrected with overrides to eleven scopes covering every section of the held text. Sections 31 and 33 are spent by their own terms: section 33 revoked EO 10798 on signing, and section 31 provided for the changeover on July 4, 1960 (the order states no other effective date, and 4 U.S.C. 2, recited in the order, fixes July 4 as the effective date of an added star). The remaining sections have no term or condition. The held Code prints the whole order as a current note, with no amendment, under 4 U.S.C. 1, and 4 U.S.C. 5 still defines the flag by reference to it. The Federal Register disposition note lists no amendment or revocation of EO 10834 itself. The order rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief and on the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949, which the Code bracket shows is now codified in chapters 1 to 11 of title 40 and division C of subtitle I of title 41; the text of those provisions is not held, so the claim relies on the Code's continued printing of the order and on 4 U.S.C. 5.
savings_reason: The design and procurement rules continue; the two spent clauses (the changeover on July 4, 1960 and the revocation of EO 10798) leave no residual command. Flags procured under earlier contracts are covered by section 25, which stays operative.
earlier_end_check: Section 31 ended on its own terms on July 4, 1960 and section 33 was performed on signing, 1959-08-21. No other section has a term, and no held later order revokes or amends EO 10834; the searches of the held corpus for the order number found the 1989 codification, the Code notes and the order's own text.
scope_check: Eleven scopes, one per section: sections 1, 2 and 3 (Part I), section 21 (sizes) and sections 22, 23, 24 and 25 (Part II), and sections 31, 32 and 33 (Part III). The attachment with the positions of the stars and proportions is part of the order but is not held in the text; sections 2 and 3 refer to it.
independent_command_check: The design provisions, the procurement and sizes rules, the definition and the two transitional clauses are independent of one another; the end of sections 31 and 33 does not affect the others.
savings_check: The transitional clauses leave no residual; the flag of EO 10798 stopped being official on July 4, 1960 when the Part I flag took its place, and section 25 continues to govern flags in possession or acquired under earlier contracts.

research_rationale: EO 12626 (Reagan, signed 1988-02-25, 53 FR 6114, published 1988-02-29) designates the Secretary of Defense as National Defense Stockpile Manager and delegates to him the functions vested in the President by the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act except those under sections 7, 8 and 13 of the Act (section 8(a) functions go to the Secretary of the Interior and section 8(b) functions to the Secretary of Agriculture) (section 1); delegates the functions under section 4(h) of the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act (section 2) and under section 204(f) of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (section 3) to the Secretary of Defense; and authorizes redelegation with consultation (section 4). The Federal Register text in the dossier inventory starts at section 1, so the authority recital (Stock Piling Act, section 3203 of Pub. L. 100-180 and 3 U.S.C. 301) is read as context. The held Code notes to 50 U.S.C. 98 print the full order as a current note and show no ending or amendment; EO 14051 of October 31, 2021, printed there, designates the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment under 50 U.S.C. 98f, the section 7 function that section 1 of EO 12626 excludes, and says nothing that revokes or amends EO 12626. The authority statutes are in force: the Stock Piling Act (50 U.S.C. 98 et seq.) and 3 U.S.C. 301 are held; section 4(h) of the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act is held in the 2024 U.S. Code edition of 15 U.S.C. 714b, which carries a note that the subsection is delegated to the Secretary of Defense by section 2 of this order; the text of former 40 U.S.C. 485(f), now 40 U.S.C. 574(d) per the Code note, is not held (see the section 3 clause). A search of the held corpus for the order number finds only its own text, the 1989 codification and Code notes.
savings_reason: The order is a set of continuing delegations with no end; nothing in the held sources revokes or amends it, so no residual exists beyond the four operative clauses.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end: no section states a term or condition, and EO 14051 does not name or revoke EO 12626 and operates on the section 7 function that EO 12626 section 1 carves out.
scope_check: Four operative scopes, one per section: section 1 (stockpile manager and Stock Piling Act delegations), section 2 (Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act section 4(h)), section 3 (Federal Property and Administrative Services Act section 204(f)) and section 4 (redelegation and consultation).
independent_command_check: Each section delegates functions under a different statute or sets the redelegation rule; they stand independently, and no held source ends any one of them.
savings_check: No ending event, so no savings question arises.

research_rationale: EO 12081 (Carter, signed 1978-09-18, 43 FR 42237, published 1978-09-20) orders, under section 329 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1440) and section 3 of the Act of October 24, 1968, that the statutory period of Vietnam hostilities that began on February 28, 1961 shall be deemed to have terminated on October 15, 1978, for the purpose of ending the period in which active-duty service qualifies for the exemptions from the usual naturalization requirements. The authority statute is in force: the held current text of 8 U.S.C. 1440(a) still provides that the Vietnam period runs from February 28, 1961 to the date designated by the President by Executive order as the date of termination of the Vietnam hostilities, and the Code prints this order as a note under 8 U.S.C. 1440 with no ending statement. The order has no own-terms end, the Federal Register disposition notes list no amendment or revocation, and the eCFR search found no hit. The designation is a standing legal fixing of the statutory period's end date (the date October 15, 1978 is the date fixed, not a date on which the order ends), so the clause is recorded as continuing.
savings_reason: The order fixes a standing date that the statute keys to; nothing in the held sources ends or amends it, so no residual exists beyond the operative clause. Naturalizations completed on service before October 15, 1978 are governed by the statute itself.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end: the order has no term or condition. The date October 15, 1978 is the stated termination date of the statutory Vietnam hostilities period, not an end of the order; the statute still points to the date designated by Executive order, and no held later order designates another date or revokes this one.
scope_check: Single operative scope: the whole sole paragraph designating the termination date of the Vietnam hostilities period for 8 U.S.C. 1440 purposes.
independent_command_check: There is one command, the designation of the termination date; the references to the two statutory authorities are recitals of authority and not separate commands.
savings_check: No ending event, so no savings question arises; the designation continues to define the end of the statutory period.
